assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle, correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable, strongly correlated platform that did not exist before. The theory of the moire flat band and its experimental realisation form a clear, original, unusually broad discovery whose impact on condensed-matter physics is already large.
assessment.attribution: The decisive pair is the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model (theory) and the Jarillo-Herrero group's 2018 correlated-insulator and superconductivity experiments. A fair three-person configuration is MacDonald for theory, Jarillo-Herrero for the experimental discovery, and Andrei for early STM and transport evidence of flat bands. Bistritzer is credited but is the junior theory author, and I leave him out with that caveat.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups worldwide within a few years, and the field has since produced fractional Chern insulators and related states. The core claims are stable. Recognition is timely, though some may argue it is early.
uncertainties: Whether Andrei or Bistritzer should be third is genuinely open, as are claims from other early flat-band work I cannot verify from the supplied text.
The origin of the superconducting pairing is still debated, so the prize would have to rest on flat bands and correlated phases rather than the pairing mechanism.
I rely on my own memory of the literature and have not independently verified the dates or priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Exact relations such as the Jarzynski equality, the Crooks fluctuation theorem and the Evans-Searles theorems tie nonequilibrium work and entropy production to equilibrium free energies, and hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium. They are a conceptual advance in statistical mechanics, central to stochastic thermodynamics and the physics of small systems, and they are simple, general and exactly stated. This is the kind of result I judge by clarity and depth.
assessment.attribution: Evans, Cohen and Morriss (1993), Jarzynski (1997) and Crooks (1998-99) are distinct, decisive contributions. The three-name set is a plausible configuration, although Gallavotti-Cohen, Evans-Searles and Kurchan's stochastic derivation have claims, and priority among them is partly a matter of taste.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified in RNA-hairpin pulling, colloidal and single-molecule experiments, and later in quantum systems. The interpretation is stable and the results are in textbooks. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Overlapping claims by Gallavotti, Cohen, Searles, Kurchan and Hatano-Sasa could make the allocation contentious.
The impact is mostly conceptual and on analysis of small systems rather than a single decisive experiment.
I cannot verify details of the priority history from the supplied entry alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and developed by Ye, reaches fractional uncertainty near 1e-18 and underpins a possible redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and searches for dark matter. It is a clean, instrument-defining advance with large, lasting consequence.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the strontium clock. Ye's group pushed it to record accuracy and many-body interrogation. The two-person credit is clear and fair, though Ye's frequency-comb contributions overlap with the 2005 prize, and other lattice-clock groups exist.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many national laboratories with consistent agreement at the 1e-18 level. Mature, with an international redefinition process under way. Timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 prize on frequency combs may weigh against Ye.
Contributions of other lattice-clock pioneers such as Ludlow and Lemonde, and ion-clock work, could complicate the credit.
The redefinition of the second has not yet taken place.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, together with the HgTe observation of edge transport, founded a field of topological phases protected by symmetry and made it central to modern condensed matter physics. Originality and lasting influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele's 2005 papers are the decisive theory, and the Molenkamp group's 2007 measurement is the decisive experiment. Hasan's ARPES work on 3D topological insulators, plus Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents, are also credited elsewhere or missing. With only three places, Hasan and the others stay out, and that remains a genuine allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in many materials and many techniques. The core concept is stable. Recognition is mature, and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: The allocation among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan and uncredited theorists such as Bernevig, Zhang, Fu and Moore is unresolved.
The 2016 prize on topological phase transitions may be seen as having partly covered the area.
I cannot verify the finer points of priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made strong light-matter coupling possible on a chip, and it is the architecture behind most superconducting quantum processors, along with dispersive readout and microwave quantum optics. The impact on quantum technology is substantial and the idea is clear and elegant.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed it in 2004 and Wallraff et al. demonstrated it in the same year, so those three are a reasonable configuration. Girvin is not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and now the base of an engineering industry. Mature scientifically. However, the 2025 prize already recognised superconducting circuit quantum effects, which affects timing and the overlap of subject matter.
uncertainties: The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits may make a second superconducting-circuit prize seem redundant.
Girvin and others are missing from the supplied credit list.
The lasting scientific, as opposed to technological, contribution is harder to separate from transmon and qubit-development work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KTHNY theory of two-dimensional melting through dislocation and disclination unbinding, with an intermediate hexatic phase, is a landmark in statistical mechanics and, as a physicist of complex systems, I value it highly. It extended the Kosterlitz-Thouless idea to a new universality class, with lasting reach into liquid crystals, colloids and soft matter.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) are the decisive contributions, and the Kosterlitz and Thouless side of the story was recognised in 2016. The three-name configuration is natural, though the 2016 prize may be thought to have covered much of the underlying idea.
assessment.maturity: Verified in colloidal and other 2D experiments and simulations, though the nature of the transition depends on the system and is still discussed in some cases. It is mature and old.
uncertainties: The 2016 prize may already be viewed as covering the topological-defect idea.
The hexatic transition's first-order versus continuous character is system dependent.
Priority between Young and others is something I cannot verify.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy landscape and folding funnel picture links protein folding to spin-glass and disordered-system physics, and explains how a heteropolymer finds its native state despite frustration. It is conceptually deep and congenial to my own interests in complex systems, and it has been influential in biophysics.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic were central to funnel theory and Dill to lattice and hydrophobic models, so the trio is plausible. Bryngelson, Go, Shakhnovich and others are not credited, which makes allocation uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Broadly accepted conceptually, but the quantitative predictive role is mixed, and the 2024 chemistry prize for protein structure prediction and design took the practical side. Its fit with a physics prize is arguable.
uncertainties: It may be seen as chemistry or biology rather than physics.
The 2024 chemistry prize partly covered the protein field.
Allocation is unclear because of uncredited early contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum computing with trapped ions and its experimental realisation gave the first practical gate scheme and one of the leading quantum-information platforms, and high-fidelity entangling gates and quantum simulation have followed. It is important, though the field has had several recent prizes.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the 1995 theory proposal, and Blatt's group demonstrated many of the key experiments, so the trio is sensible. Wineland, Monroe and Haroche have received or overlap with earlier recognition, and Wineland's 2012 prize reduces the room.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely reproduced and independent across groups. Its timing is acceptable, but overlap with the 2012 and 2022 quantum-information prizes weighs on it.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 prize and the 2022 quantum-information prize.
Cirac and Zoller are also credited for the optical-lattice candidate, so a combined configuration might be preferred.
Experimental credit beyond Blatt, for example Monroe or Wineland, is not in the credited list.
